dialogues.speaker: Shemyakin
dialogues.text: ...I already told you, my friend lives in Port Belovodye. I'll stay with him for a while, so don't worry about me. Just change my ticket, please.

dialogues.speaker: Voskresensky
dialogues.text: I understand your situation, but rules are rules. Neither of your parents is here, and I can't simply change a child's ticket on his own say-so.

dialogues.speaker: Shemyakin
dialogues.text: Sir, surely you saw them fighting just now. They're not coming back anytime soon.

dialogues.speaker: Shemyakin
dialogues.text: I know them all too well. They probably both think the other one's watching me. So, am I just supposed to sit here forever while you and I eye each other?

dialogues.speaker: Voskresensky
dialogues.text: But rules are rules. What if something happens to you on the way to Port Belovodye... Well, of course, we want every passenger to have a safe trip.

dialogues.speaker: Voskresensky
dialogues.text: But if anything did happen, that responsibility would fall on me.

dialogues.speaker: Voskresensky
dialogues.text: So why don't you wait here on the platform for now? They might come looking for you soon. Parents love their children. I'm sure they wouldn't just leave you here.

dialogues.speaker: Shemyakin
dialogues.text: I used to think parents don't stop liking each other either. That is, until I learned that mine had found people they liked better. Ha.
